question: Can the minimum representation dimension needed for a specified prediction task be inferred by preserving mutual information between paired views, and can a hybrid neural critic plus a one-shot cross-covariance participation ratio recover that dimension from finite, noisy, high-dimensional data?

key_findings.claim: The paper operationalizes task-relevant dimension as the smallest paired-view bottleneck that preserves the mutual information shared by predictor X and target Y.
key_findings.evidence: Two encoders g^X and g^Y map paired high-dimensional observations into k_z dimensions; the proposed target is the smallest k_z at which I(g^X(X);g^Y(Y)) saturates to I(X;Y), thereby discarding variation private to either view rather than reconstructing the observations.

key_findings.claim: The hybrid critic decouples encoder bottleneck size from cross-view critic expressivity, correcting a concrete failure of dot-product critics.
key_findings.evidence: A separable critic T=g^X(x)·g^Y(y) forces all dependence into a bilinear form; the hybrid retains k_z-dimensional encoders but applies a flexible head T_theta([g^X(x),g^Y(y)]). On a K_Z=4 joint Gaussian, separable saturation occurs at K_Z+1 while hybrid saturation occurs at K_Z; on an eight-component K_Z=1 mixture the separable estimate inflates much further while hybrid again saturates at one.

anchors.section: D.1 Non-invertibility of the Gaussian mixture, Figure 12

key_findings.claim: The Gaussian theory proves a limitation of the standard critic family, but it does not prove general dimensional recovery by the hybrid critic.
key_findings.evidence: For jointly Gaussian variables the exact optimal critic contains bilinear cross terms and self-quadratic terms; K+2 separable coordinates suffice constructively and an augmented quadratic critic works in K. The observed K+1 sufficiency is explained analytically only for K=1 to within 0.04 bits and extrapolated through a hyperspherical ansatz; the appendix explicitly says K>1 is not shown.

anchors.section: A.2.1 Derivation of the Optimal Gaussian Critic
A.2.2 Choice of architecture and optimal embeddings

key_findings.claim: The one-shot estimator trains an overparameterized hybrid model and converts the singular values of the learned cross-view embedding covariance into a participation-ratio dimension.
key_findings.evidence: With centered cross-covariance C_XY and singular values sigma_i, the paper defines d_eff=(sum_i sigma_i)^2/sum_i sigma_i^2. At fixed k_z=64 it tracks Gaussian K_Z over the tested signal and batch regimes, and variance across ten trials falls after k_z exceeds the true dimension.

anchors.section: 3.3 Single-shot dimensionality estimation via participation ratio, Equation 4

key_findings.claim: The reported d_eff is not identifiable from the hybrid InfoNCE objective because the unwhitened cross-covariance spectrum has a latent-coordinate gauge freedom.
key_findings.evidence: Invertibly rescaling or mixing encoder coordinates can change the singular values and their participation ratio, while the first layer of the flexible hybrid head can apply the inverse transform and leave every critic score—and hence InfoNCE—unchanged. The method applies neither whitening/canonical correlation nor output normalization or another gauge constraint before computing C_XY.

anchors.section: 3.3 Single-shot dimensionality estimation via participation ratio

key_findings.claim: Participation ratio measures strength-weighted effective rank, not necessarily a discrete latent, topological, or minimal sufficient dimension.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B.2 states there is no a priori reason to prefer singular-value PR; eigenvalue PR suppresses weak modes more and spectral entropy inflates them. Figure 9 shows different scalar dimensions for unequal singular values, while the Gaussian benchmarks distribute a fixed total MI equally across factors, making each direction weaker as K_Z rises and causing undercounting when signal or batch size is insufficient.

key_findings.claim: Finite-data recovery is promising on the synthetic teachers but depends on selecting a model with held-out data and then reporting an in-sample quantity.
key_findings.evidence: The max-test/train-estimate rule chooses t*=argmax_t I_test(t), then reports I_train(t*) and computes training cross-covariance at that checkpoint. Around 10^3 training examples recover K_Z=4 Gaussian and K_Z=1 mixture cases, but the test set has only 128 samples in the finite synthetic protocol and is reused over epochs for selection.

key_findings.claim: The noise comparison is a change of estimand, not a like-for-like demonstration that classical intrinsic-dimension estimators fail at the same target.
key_findings.evidence: With additive full-dimensional noise, Levina-Bickel MLE and Two-NN estimate the geometry of each noisy observation cloud, whose intrinsic dimension legitimately approaches the ambient 500; the paired method instead estimates cross-view shared signal and stays near K_Z on N=16,384 samples. The authors acknowledge that this behavior is expected.

anchors.section: 3.2 Noise in the observation space and intrinsic dimensionality
C.2 Comparing with intrinsic dimensionality estimators, Figure 11

key_findings.claim: Mutual-information preservation alone does not uniquely define a minimum Euclidean latent dimension without regularity and model-class assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: The definition minimizes coordinate count while using expressive deterministic neural encoders, but does not impose continuity, bi-Lipschitzness, topology preservation, decoder sufficiency, or a fixed function class. Arbitrary recodings can preserve information in different coordinate dimensions; the discussion itself says the estimate depends on view construction and embedding-network architecture.

key_findings.claim: The Ising experiment recovers a visually coherent finite-size collapse, but it inserts the known critical parameters rather than estimating them blind.
key_findings.evidence: For L=13 to 133 and 10,000 configurations at each (L,T), d_eff curves are plotted against the standard scaling variable using the exact T_c≈2.269 and fixed nu=1; MI peaks near T_c and d_eff is about one in the ordered phase before increasing with domain structure. Thus the experiment validates compatibility with known scaling, not independent discovery of T_c or nu.

key_findings.claim: The claim that Ising dimensionality is not an architecture or tuning artifact is stronger than the supplied controls.
key_findings.evidence: Only the same generic MLP/PR pipeline and one spatial split are shown; there is no alternative encoder, PR definition, split geometry, critic, stopping rule, or baseline phase-transition estimator. Moreover, Appendix D displays d_eff only where estimated MI exceeds 0.5 bits, a selective reliability threshold omitted from the main claim.

anchors.section: D.3 2D Ising model, MI reliability threshold

key_findings.claim: The Ising paired-view conditional-independence justification is questionable for adjacent regions of an interacting lattice.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix C asserts that the two spatial domains are conditionally independent given a shared latent state Z, yet nearest-neighbor boundary interactions directly couple the regions and no explicit finite Z is constructed or conditioned upon. Changing the split or interface therefore changes both MI and the dimension being measured.

anchors.section: C.1 View splitting for intrinsic dimensionality estimation

key_findings.claim: The pendulum study approaches the expected phase-space dimensions, but the headline 'as few as a hundred samples' counts trajectories rather than the paired examples seen during training.
key_findings.evidence: Each 60-frame trajectory produces 57 overlapping past/future pairs; therefore 100 initial conditions yield 5,700 paired training examples, not 100. With more trajectories, the single pendulum approaches d_eff≈2 and the double approaches 4 over ten trials.

key_findings.claim: The pendulum result does not use the paper's stated standard pipeline and is materially sensitive to an unspecified stopping hyperparameter.
key_findings.evidence: Unlike synthetic/Ising runs, pendulum uses tied encoders, LayerNorm in the critic, batch 256 rather than 128, 200-400 epochs, and earliest attainment of a fixed fraction of maximum test MI rather than max-test. The main text never gives that fraction; Figure 17 shows late stopping inflates the single estimate toward 3 and only near-maximum stopping brings the double estimate close to 4.

anchors.section: F.2 Pendulum dynamics, Model Architecture and Training Protocol

key_findings.claim: The pendulum application sits in tension with the paper's own requirement for independent observation noise.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix C calls uncorrelated observation noise a requirement because deterministic invertible views can make continuous MI diverge or become parameterization dependent. Appendix F describes deterministic adjacent video frames and no independent observation-noise model, while InfoNCE is near its 8-bit batch ceiling; the recovered dimension can therefore reflect finite precision, estimator saturation, and chosen stopping rather than the stipulated shared-noisy-view model.

anchors.section: C.1 View splitting for intrinsic dimensionality estimation
F.2 Pendulum dynamics, Training Protocol and Stopping

key_findings.claim: The physical-case evidence is a pair of controlled benchmarks, not yet a validated scientific instrument for unknown experimental systems.
key_findings.evidence: Ising is simulated with known T_c and exponent; pendulum data are reused from a prior dataset with known 2D/4D targets and no acquisition/noise audit here. No correlated noise, hidden nuisance, misspecified views, nonstationarity, unknown ground truth, or prospective discovery is tested.

anchors.section: 3.5 Estimating task-relevant dimensionality of physics datasets

method.core_idea: Treat dimensionality as task-specific shared information: learn low-dimensional representations of paired views with a contrastive MI objective, make the critic expressive after rather than inside the bottleneck, and read the effective number of shared embedding modes from one overparameterized model.
method.mechanism: Independent encoders map X and Y to k_z-dimensional embeddings. A one-hidden-layer hybrid head receives their concatenation and is trained with symmetrized InfoNCE, avoiding the dot-product critic's need to spend coordinates representing nonlinear interactions. For a sweep-based estimate, choose the first k_z at which MI saturates. For the proposed one-shot estimate, train at k_z=64, center the paired encoder outputs, take singular values of their cross-covariance, and report their participation ratio. Finite datasets select a checkpoint by maximum held-out MI but report training MI/covariance; physics cases create views by a spatial Ising split or past/future video stacks.
assumptions: The task can be represented by paired views whose shared dependence excludes irrelevant variation and whose construction is scientifically meaningful.
The learned MI lower bound is sufficiently accurate to detect saturation and distinguish weak shared modes.
The encoder and hybrid-head classes can represent a minimal sufficient shared latent without introducing architecture-dependent dimension.
An overparameterized bottleneck known to exceed the unknown target can be selected in advance.
The unwhitened embedding cross-covariance spectrum is a stable, meaningful representation of shared latent geometry despite latent-coordinate non-identifiability.
Singular-value participation ratio is the appropriate strength-weighted scalar dimension for the scientific target.
Training examples and batches are large enough to resolve every relevant direction, including weak factors.
Held-out checkpoint selection followed by training-set estimation controls overfitting without material selection bias.
For intrinsic-dimension use, two views share a latent state and have sufficiently independent private observation noise.
MCMC configurations are sufficiently decorrelated and pendulum overlapping frame pairs supply an effective sample size close to their nominal count.

techniques.role: Defines relevance through mutual information preserved jointly across compressed predictor and target views.
Provides the contrastive neural lower bound optimized throughout most experiments.
Retains explicit encoder bottlenecks while using a flexible concatenated MLP head for nonlinear cross-view interaction.
Infers dimension from the smallest k_z beyond which optimized MI ceases to rise.
Soft-counts singular modes of paired encoder embeddings to obtain a one-model effective dimension.
Chooses an epoch by maximum held-out MI while reporting MI and representation spectrum on training data.
Creates paired views from a single object using spatial domains or past/future frames.
Maps known low-dimensional Gaussian, mixture, hypersphere, and Swiss-roll latents into 500 observed dimensions.
Derives the Gaussian optimal critic and isolates missing self-quadratic terms in a dot-product architecture.
Tests whether Ising MI and d_eff curves collapse using known critical parameters.

evaluations.setting: Infinite-resampling K=500 observations from a K_Z=4 joint Gaussian with 2 bits total MI, under frozen linear and one-hidden-layer nonlinear teacher maps; ten trials.
evaluations.metric: MI saturation location k_z* and estimated MI versus bottleneck size.
evaluations.result: Hybrid critic saturates at k_z*=4 for both observation maps and estimates roughly the true 2 bits; separable critic saturates at 5.
evaluations.baseline: CCA succeeds only for the linear observation map and produces spurious/non-saturating behavior after the nonlinear map; standard separable InfoNCE overestimates dimension by one.

evaluations.setting: Infinite-resampling K=500 observations from an eight-component nonlinear Gaussian mixture with true K_Z=1, ring radius 2, and within-component correlation about 0.97; ten trials.
evaluations.metric: MI saturation dimension and one-shot d_eff.
evaluations.result: Hybrid critic saturates at one and its PR is near one.
evaluations.baseline: Separable critic requires roughly eight embedding coordinates to saturate and has d_eff about seven in Appendix Figure 12; nonlinear CCA fails.

evaluations.setting: Shared or paired synthetic latents passed through nonlinear K=500 teachers with independent additive white observation noise.
evaluations.result: Noise reduces estimated MI but hybrid saturation and d_eff remain controlled by K_Z over the plotted range.
evaluations.baseline: Levina-Bickel MLE and Two-NN estimates rise toward the ambient dimension, while targeting each noisy view's geometry rather than cross-view shared signal.

evaluations.setting: One-shot joint-Gaussian sweeps with fixed k_z=64, K=500, total MI and batch size varied.
evaluations.metric: Cross-covariance singular-value PR versus true K_Z.
evaluations.result: d_eff tracks K_Z while each latent direction has adequate signal and batch coverage; variance across ten trials decreases with overparameterization.
evaluations.baseline: At batch size 128 or low MI per direction, higher-dimensional targets are undercounted; the sweep-based k_z* method requires many models.

evaluations.setting: Finite fixed nonlinear-teacher datasets, k_z=64, 100 epochs, and a 128-sample held-out set.
evaluations.result: Both K_Z=4 Gaussian and K_Z=1 mixture examples converge near the correct dimension at approximately 10^3 training examples; larger N extends the recoverable K_Z range.
evaluations.baseline: Smaller datasets or lower MI per dimension fail to resolve all latent directions.

evaluations.setting: Noisy Gaussian latent benchmark with N=16,384, K=500, and K_Z varied; ten trials.
evaluations.result: Paired-view hybrid PR stays near K_Z over the tested noise range.
evaluations.baseline: Scikit-dimension Levina-Bickel MLE and Two-NN, averaged across X/Y estimates, increase sharply with noise toward the noisy observation dimension.

evaluations.setting: 2D nearest-neighbor Ising MCMC at J=1, h=0, L=13-133, T=0-4.5, 10,000 configurations per (L,T), ten training trials, and a fixed spatial split.
evaluations.metric: Estimated MI, d_eff, and collapse against the known finite-size variable using T_c≈2.269 and nu=1.
evaluations.result: MI peaks near T_c; d_eff approaches about one below T_c, increases around the critical region, and the curves visually collapse across L under the prescribed scaling.
evaluations.baseline: Known Ising critical parameters and theoretical leading scalings; no learned-exponent, alternative-split, or alternative-architecture baseline.

evaluations.setting: Single-pendulum grayscale 128x128 video; up to 1,000 training trajectories, 57 overlapping pairs per trajectory, tied encoders, batch 256, ten trials.
evaluations.metric: d_eff versus trajectory count and stopping fraction.
evaluations.result: The estimate approaches the expected phase-space dimension 2 with sufficient trajectories, but at late/maximum stopping it inflates toward roughly 2.6-3.
evaluations.baseline: Known state (theta, angular velocity), dimension 2; prior autoencoder method is described as brittle but is not rerun in a matched table.

evaluations.setting: Rigid double-pendulum grayscale video under the same paired-frame construction; up to 1,000 trajectories and ten trials.
evaluations.metric: d_eff versus trajectory count and stopping fraction.
evaluations.result: The estimate rises toward the expected dimension 4, reaching it only near the maximum-MI stopping threshold in Appendix Figure 17; around 100 trajectories it remains below four.
evaluations.baseline: Known state (two angles and two angular velocities), dimension 4.

evaluations.setting: Alternative one-shot dimension functionals applied to unequal two-mode spectra.
evaluations.metric: Singular-value PR, eigenvalue PR, spectral-entropy dimension, and intermediate power PR.
evaluations.result: All equal two only when the modes are equal; eigenvalue PR drops faster as one weakens and spectral entropy counts weak modes more strongly.
evaluations.baseline: No unique ground-truth scalar for unequal relevance strengths; the paper chooses singular-value PR as a middle ground without an a priori justification.

limitations: Author-stated: success depends on accurate MI estimation, view construction, embedding-network architecture, and enough samples to resolve latent structure; formal success/failure conditions remain open.
Author-stated: there is no a priori reason to prefer the selected singular-value participation ratio over other effective-rank functionals.
Author-stated: InfoNCE saturates at log2(batch size); in the pendulum regime this is about 8 bits and may require larger batches or alternative bounds.
Author-stated: prolonged pendulum training inflates d_eff, and modality-tailored encoders may be needed beyond the tested generic MLP.

Reviewer inference: the one-shot d_eff is not invariant to invertible rescaling/mixing of encoder coordinates even though the hybrid critic objective is, leaving the estimate unidentifiable without whitening or a gauge constraint.
Reviewer inference: MI preservation alone does not identify a unique minimal Euclidean coordinate dimension without continuity, topology, sufficiency, and function-class assumptions.
Reviewer inference: an overparameterized k_z must be chosen larger than an unknown target, weakening the literal 'one-shot' characterization and creating a hidden upper-bound assumption.

Reviewer inference: max-test/train-estimate repeatedly selects on a set called test and then reports a training quantity, permitting selection and in-sample optimism; a separate validation and untouched test split are absent.

Reviewer inference: synthetic benchmarks use favorable low-dimensional teachers, equally distributed Gaussian MI, independent white noise, and known targets; correlated/shared nuisance and weak unequal factors are untested.
Reviewer inference: most numerical results are plots without tabulated estimates, intervals, calibration criteria, or preregistered tolerances for declaring correct dimension.
Reviewer inference: Ising uses known T_c and nu for collapse and hides d_eff where MI<=0.5 bits; it does not blindly discover critical parameters.

Reviewer inference: Ising burn-in length, sweeps between samples, replica count, autocorrelation/effective sample size, and convergence diagnostics are not numerically specified, which is important near critical slowing down.
Reviewer inference: pendulum changes architecture, batch size, training duration, and stopping rule, and the decisive fraction-of-maximum threshold is not specified in the main result.
Reviewer inference: 57 overlapping pairs per trajectory are correlated, so nominal pair count overstates effective sample size while the headline counts only trajectories.

Reviewer inference: the physics tests have known answers and no prospective unknown-system validation, independent acquisition audit, correlated measurement noise, nonstationarity, or real-sensor nuisance study.
failure_modes: An invertible coordinate rescaling can change d_eff while leaving all hybrid critic scores and InfoNCE unchanged.
Weak but task-relevant modes are downweighted by PR and can disappear as total MI is spread across more factors.
Insufficient batch size or finite samples undercount latent dimension even when the representation architecture is adequate.
A separable dot-product critic spends extra coordinates on self-normalization or multimodal dependence and inflates the inferred dimension.
A test set reused for epoch selection can favor a noise maximum; reporting training MI/covariance at that epoch compounds optimism.
Runs that learn no nontrivial MI are discarded, which can condition reported accuracy on optimizer success without a failure-rate denominator.
Correlated observation noise or shared nuisance variables enter both views and are counted as task-relevant structure.
Noiseless deterministic paired views can make continuous MI divergent or parameterization dependent, undermining saturation-based interpretation.
InfoNCE ceiling effects and prolonged training inflate pendulum d_eff; the stopping fraction can move the answer toward or away from known ground truth.
Different spatial/temporal view splits change which information is shared and therefore change the reported 'dimension.'
Near-critical Ising autocorrelation can make nominally 10,000 configurations far fewer effective independent samples if sweep spacing is insufficient.
Classical intrinsic-dimension baselines can appear to fail simply because they estimate the noisy observation manifold rather than paired shared signal.
reusable_insights: Separate representation bottleneck dimension from critic expressivity; otherwise architecture rank is mistaken for data dimension.
Define dimensionality relative to a prediction/view task and state explicitly what private and shared variation the view construction includes.
Before using a learned embedding spectrum, audit invariance under latent-coordinate transformations and impose whitening, canonical-correlation normalization, or another identifiable gauge.
Report a spectrum and sensitivity across effective-rank functionals instead of presenting one PR scalar as a unique dimension.
Use distinct train, validation, and untouched test sets for neural MI checkpointing, and quantify selection bias by nested resampling.
Treat batch size, MI per factor, and effective independent sample size as resolution limits for weak latent modes.
Compare estimators only when their estimands match: noisy observation-manifold dimension is not shared-signal dimension.
For physics validation, estimate critical parameters blind and test alternative view splits, encoders, critics, and stopping rules before claiming physical discovery.
Count both independent experimental units and correlated pairs/windows when describing sample efficiency.
Stress-test with correlated noise, shared nuisance, unequal factor strengths, misspecified views, noninvertible observations, and unknown ground truth.
open_questions: Can a whitened cross-covariance or canonical-correlation effective rank yield an objective-invariant, identifiable one-shot dimension?
Under what continuity, topology, sufficiency, and encoder-class conditions does MI saturation equal a minimal latent dimension?
How can k_z be chosen demonstrably above an unknown target without a sweep or a priori upper bound?
What calibrated uncertainty interval and decision rule should accompany a non-integer PR estimate?
How does the estimator behave when latent directions carry highly unequal MI or only rare-event predictive information?
What is the effect of correlated sensor noise, shared confounders, nonstationarity, and overlapping temporal windows?
Does nested validation remove max-test/train-estimate optimism while retaining the reported sample efficiency?
Can the method recover T_c and nu from Ising data without supplying them and remain stable across spatial partitions?
How many effective independent Ising configurations remain after accounting for MCMC autocorrelation near T_c?
Which pendulum stopping threshold produced the main Figure 6 result, and would a threshold selected without known ground truth recover both systems?
Does the method make correct prospective discoveries on genuinely unknown experimental systems and independent sensor datasets?

competitive_landscape.title: Data Efficiency, Dimensionality Reduction, and the Generalized Symmetric Information Bottleneck
competitive_landscape.difference: GSIB already frames simultaneous compression of two variables as preserving their shared information and derives data-efficiency advantages, so the paired-view SIB formulation is not new here. The target paper turns it into a neural dimension estimator and adds critic/participation-ratio diagnostics.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v2, revised 2 February 2024; current on 23 August 2026

competitive_landscape.title: Accurate Estimation of Mutual Information in High Dimensional Data
competitive_landscape.difference: This same-group work develops reliability checks, bias correction, confidence intervals, probabilistic critics, and the max-test/train-estimate family for high-dimensional MI. The target paper reuses the stopping logic but asks for latent dimension and introduces a hybrid bottleneck plus spectrum; it omits many of the later v3 reliability safeguards.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v3, revised 10 June 2026; current on 23 August 2026

competitive_landscape.title: Approximating Mutual Information of High-Dimensional Variables Using Learned Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Latent MI learns low-dimensional representations and then applies a nonparametric estimator, scaling beyond 1,000 observed dimensions and demonstrating biological applications. The target paper instead embeds MI estimation and dimension inference in one hybrid contrastive model, but has only known-answer physics cases and an unidentifiable raw embedding spectrum.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 3 September 2024; current on 23 August 2026 and corresponding to the NeurIPS 2024 proceedings paper

competitive_landscape.title: Simultaneous Dimensionality Reduction: A Data Efficient Approach for Multimodal Representations Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: The TMLR paper compares simultaneous methods such as PLS/CCA against independent PCA-style reduction and shows that shared covariance can be recovered more sample-efficiently. It is primarily linear and estimates covarying structure; the target paper extends to nonlinear neural MI and a task-relevant scalar dimension.
competitive_landscape.source_version: TMLR camera-ready record, published and last modified 4 October 2024; current on 23 August 2026

competitive_landscape.title: Compressed Predictive Information Coding
competitive_landscape.difference: CPIC already compresses past and future views while maximizing predictive information and recovers latent spaces of noisy dynamical systems. It optimizes useful representations rather than estimating their minimal dimension via critic saturation/PR, but it contains much of the past-future information-bottleneck combination used in the pendulum case.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 3 March 2022; current on 23 August 2026

competitive_landscape.title: Automated Discovery of Fundamental Variables Hidden in Experimental Data
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct physical latent-dimension competitor and dataset antecedent
competitive_landscape.difference: Chen et al. infer the number and candidate identities of state variables from high-dimensional physical videos and supply the pendulum dataset reused here. The target method avoids reconstruction and uses past-future MI, which can focus on task relevance, but it does not independently rerun a matched baseline or show unknown-system discovery.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Nature Computational Science version of record, published 25 July 2022; current on 23 August 2026

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The work introduces task-relevant dimension as a paired-view MI-preservation problem, identifies systematic dimension inflation from separable critics, replaces them with a hybrid bottleneck/concatenated critic, and reads dimension in one shot from the learned cross-covariance spectrum.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The separable failure is derived concretely for Gaussian optimal critics and reproduced on Gaussian and multimodal teachers; the hybrid recovers known bottleneck saturation points across those cases. A fixed k_z=64 participation ratio works over synthetic signal, noise, batch, and sample-size sweeps and yields physically plausible Ising and pendulum trends.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The SIB framing, simultaneous paired-view reduction, predictive-information compression, learned low-dimensional MI, and video state-variable discovery all have direct primary antecedents. The credible narrower novelty is the specific combination of an explicit neural bottleneck with a flexible joint head, plus one-model cross-covariance PR for dimension. No checked prior primary source contained that full combination. However, the core one-shot scalar is not invariant under the hybrid model's latent-coordinate gauge and therefore is not identified by its training objective; the paper establishes empirical recovery under a favorable architectural/optimizer convention, not a general geometry-preservation theorem. Physics evidence is confirmatory and hyperparameter-sensitive. Novelty is methodologically meaningful but the strongest general and scientific-instrument claims require a whitened/invariant estimator, blind validation, and matched competitors.

reviewer_notes: Complete primary-source review of all 30 indexed PDF pages: main text pages 1-8, references pages 9-12, and Appendices A-F pages 13-30, including every displayed derivation, figure, caption, and experimental detail. Rendered page images were additionally inspected for pages 4, 6, 7, 8, 21, 23, 24, 27, 29, and 30 to resolve Equations 4/36-39, Figures 4-6/9-12/15-17, curve trends, thresholds, and physical protocols. Graph-read values are explicitly approximate; exact settings and counts are transcribed from captions/text. Current target record checked on the official arXiv primary page on 2026-08-23: arXiv:2602.08105v1, submitted 8 February 2026, matches the indexed source pin. A later official PMLR 326 workshop record dated 26 April 2026 was also noted but was not substituted for the indexed arXiv full-text source. Competitor verification used at least three independent query families: (1) task-relevant/predictive latent dimension plus information bottleneck; (2) neural high-dimensional MI, joint/hybrid/separable critics, learned bottlenecks, and effective rank; (3) paired-view/multimodal simultaneous dimensionality reduction and shared-signal noise robustness; (4) physical state-variable discovery, pendulum videos, Ising criticality, and predictive information. Six direct current primary records from official arXiv, OpenReview/TMLR, NeurIPS-linked arXiv, and the publisher were opened and version/date pinned. Combination audit found prior SIB, simultaneous reduction, predictive-information coding, learned-representation MI, and pendulum latent discovery, but not the exact hybrid-critic plus cross-covariance-PR one-shot combination. Contradiction audit covers latent-gauge non-identifiability, PR-versus-dimension semantics, test-selection/in-sample estimation, different-estimand baseline comparisons, inserted Ising critical parameters, the MI>0.5 display filter, trajectory-versus-pair sample counts, pendulum protocol changes and unstated stopping fraction, and the noiseless-view tension. Provenance fields reproduce the indexed source record exactly.
